memories.content: Data caveat: Saturday 2024-07-27 data starts at 11:57 (13 hours covered), missing midnight–11:56. Wednesday 2024-07-31 has full 24-hour coverage.

Data caveat: Wednesday 2024-07-31 is a summer weekday with typical commuter patterns; Saturday is a summer weekend with different travel profiles (e.g., airport trips may shift to leisure/tourist patterns).
Data caveat: Weather data for Saturday shows 0.0 mm precip; however, microclimate or timing-specific conditions (e.g., afternoon heat) were not tested.
Data caveat: Saturday 2024-07-27 coverage starts at 11:57, missing 00:00–11:56. Wednesday 2024-07-31 has full 24h coverage.
Data caveat: The analyst's comparison of Saturday to 'other July 2024 Saturdays' (H4 scope note) is not tested by the provided queries; only the two specific days are compared.

Finding for 'Why was taxi demand on Saturday 2024-07-27 so much lower than on Wednesday 2024-07-31?': The apparent demand drop is primarily a data coverage artifact: Saturday 2024-07-27 only has 13 hours of trip data (11:57–23:59) vs 24 hours for Wednesday 2024-07-31, missing the early-morning hours entirely. -> Saturday 2024-07-27 had fewer total trips (59957 vs 98655) and fewer airport trips (6100 vs 10068) compared to Wednesday 2024-07-31. However, Saturday's trips per hour (4612.1) is higher than Wednesday's (4110.6), indicating the lower total trip count is consistent with the 13-hour vs 24-hour coverage gap rather than lower per-hour demand. (evidence Q6)

Finding for 'Why was taxi demand on Saturday 2024-07-27 so much lower than on Wednesday 2024-07-31?': Even after hourly normalization, Saturdays in July 2024 have intrinsically lower demand than Wednesdays due to day-of-week patterns (e.g., fewer commuters, different leisure timing). -> Saturday shows the highest average hourly trips (4612.1) among all days, exceeding Wednesday (4110.6) and all other weekdays. The range of hourly trips on Saturday (221 to 5548) overlaps significantly with other days, indicating no intrinsic lower demand. Sunday has the lowest average (3157.0), but Saturday's demand is clearly higher, not lower, after hourly normalization. (evidence Q3)

Finding for 'Why was taxi demand on Saturday 2024-07-27 so much lower than on Wednesday 2024-07-31?': Weather on 2024-07-27 (e.g., heavy rain or extreme heat) suppressed taxi demand relative to 2024-07-31. -> Saturday 2024-07-27 had no precipitation (0.0 mm) and clear weather (wmo_code 3), while Wednesday 2024-07-31 had 9.9 mm of rain and overcast conditions (wmo_code 63). Despite the less favorable weather on Wednesday (rain), it had 65% more total trips and 11% fewer trips per hour than Saturday, indicating weather was not the suppressing factor for Saturday demand. (evidence Q4)

Finding for 'Why was taxi demand on Saturday 2024-07-27 so much lower than on Wednesday 2024-07-31?': Airport-related trips (which are high-volume) were unusually low on 2024-07-27 vs 2024-07-31, driving the overall gap. -> Saturday 2024-07-27 had fewer total trips (59957 vs 98655) and fewer airport trips (6100 vs 10068) compared to Wednesday 2024-07-31. However, when normalized by hours covered, Saturday's trips per hour (4612.1) is higher than Wednesday's (4110.6), and airport trips per hour are also higher on Saturday (469.2 vs 419.5). The gap in total trips is consistent with the difference in hours covered (13 vs 24), suggesting the lower airport trip count is a consequence of reduced data coverage rather than disproportionately low demand. (evidence Q7)

Finding for 'Why was taxi demand on Saturday 2024-07-27 so much lower than on Wednesday 2024-07-31?': The lower airport trip count on Saturday is entirely due to the 13-hour coverage gap, not lower demand per hour. -> Saturday 2024-07-27 had fewer total trips (59957 vs 98655) and fewer airport trips (6100 vs 10068) compared to Wednesday 2024-07-31. However, when normalized by hours covered, Saturday's trips per hour (4612.1) is higher than Wednesday's (4110.6), and airport trips per hour are also higher on Saturday (469.2 vs 419.5). The gap in total trips is consistent with the difference in hours covered (13 vs 24), suggesting the lower airport trip count is a consequence of reduced data coverage rather than disproportionately low demand. (evidence Q8)
